coverage.scope: Comprehensive UVTA Appendix §1 definitions, §§2 insolvency, 3 value/foreclosure, 4 actual and financial-risk fraud, 5 present creditor and insider debt, 6 transfers made, 7 remedies, 8 defenses and subsequent transfers, 9 extinguishment, 10 choice law, 12/13 supplementary and uniformity, 15 title

topics.title: D Appendix: UVTA §1–§3 Core Definitions, Insolvency and Value
topics.description: The actual statutory criteria, not merely the general fraud summary.

entries.title: §1(2) Asset means unencumbered, nonexempt property
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Asset excludes property to extent subject to VALID lien, property generally exempt outside bankruptcy, qualifying entirety interest unreachable by one spouse's creditors.
entries.laymanExplanation: Secured half of house is not free debtor asset for state UVTA analysis.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish federal §548 'interest in property' from state §1 asset definition.
entries.examApplication: Analyze equity and whether existing lien valid.
entries.examTrap: Do not value collateral gross without subtracting valid lien when UVTA specifies asset.

entries.title: §1(3) claim includes contingent, disputed, unmatured
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: State fraudulent transfer claimant includes right to payment regardless judgment, liquidated status, contingency, maturity, dispute, law or equity, secured or unsecured; broad 'creditor' = holder claim.
entries.laymanExplanation: You can be a creditor even before invoice due or verdict entered.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinguish §544(b)'s actual unsecured creditor special federal trigger.
entries.examApplication: Determine claim date for present vs future standing.
entries.examTrap: A person not yet entitled to any payment is not automatically present creditor.

entries.title: §1(6)/(8) debtor and insider
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Debtor person liable on claim; insider includes relatives of individual/partners, officers/directors/person controlling corporation, certain affiliated businesses and their insiders, managing agents. Affiliate can turn on 20% voting interest or substantial control.
entries.laymanExplanation: Transfers to mother, controlling officer, sibling business can trigger insider red flags/§5(b).
entries.legalExplanation: §1(1) affiliate identifies 20%-vote interownership and lease/control relationships, with exclusions for security-only holdings.
entries.examApplication: Map actors and indirect control, not only formal title.
entries.examTrap: Any friend isn't automatically statutory insider.

entries.title: §1(9),(16),(17): lien, transfer and valid lien
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Transfer includes direct/indirect, voluntary/involuntary dispositions of assets or interests including payment, release, lease, license, encumbrance; lien includes agreement, judicial process and statute; valid lien must defeat later lien creditor.
entries.laymanExplanation: Even granting security interest or forgiving a debt can be transfer.
entries.legalExplanation: Applicable state priority decides 'valid lien'.
entries.examApplication: Identify borrower lien encumbrance as transfer even if no cash physically leaves.
entries.examTrap: Valid lien test matters for UVTA 'asset' net value.

entries.title: UVTA §2 balance-sheet insolvency, presumption for nonpayment
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Debtor insolvent if debts > assets at FAIR valuation; generally failing to pay debts as due (except bona fide dispute) presumes insolvency unless rebutted. Exclude concealed/fraudulently transferred assets and secured obligations matched to excluded assets under specified §2(c),(d).
entries.laymanExplanation: If liabilities $800k exceed qualifying assets $600k, balance-sheet insolvent; regular unpaid bills provide rebuttable shortcut.
entries.legalExplanation: §2(b) shifts presumption by putting burden of proving noninsolvency more probable on other side.
entries.examApplication: For each hypothetical distinguish measured asset types, disputed debt and rebuttal.
entries.examTrap: Don't equate nonpayment of one genuinely disputed invoice to general nonpayment presumption.

entries.title: UVTA §3(a): value includes property and satisfaction/security of antecedent debt
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Value given if property transferred or antecedent debt secured/satisfied, but unperformed extraordinary promise of support outside ordinary business NOT value.
entries.laymanExplanation: Paying valid old debt can be full value even if it disadvantages other creditors.
entries.legalExplanation: Separate UVTA insider preference §5(b) from ordinary constructively fraudulent no-value transfers.
entries.examApplication: Identify what debtor received, not beneficiary's happy reaction.
entries.examTrap: A vague promise to support child someday may be excluded.

entries.title: UVTA §3(b): regularly conducted foreclosure safe harbor
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: For constructive voidability under UVTA §§4(a)(2),5, properly conducted noncollusive foreclosure or power-of-sale under mortgage/trust/security agreement conclusively provides reasonably equivalent value.
entries.laymanExplanation: Legally run foreclosure can satisfy value despite discount compared to appraisal.
entries.legalExplanation: This is EXPRESS state model statutory rule unlike federal BFP majority's construction.
entries.examApplication: Compare BFP v RTC and §548; analyze actual adopted statute.
entries.examTrap: Not safe harbor for collusive or unlawful sale or necessarily actual-fraud §4(a)(1).

entries.title: UVTA §3(c): present value/substantial contemporaneity
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Present value when parties intended exchange to be contemporaneous and actually substantially contemporaneous.
entries.laymanExplanation: A genuine cash-for-goods exchange is different from paying old invoice.
entries.legalExplanation: Useful in §8 defenses and comparisons with preference §547(c)(1).
entries.examApplication: Distinguish present value and antecedent debt.
entries.examTrap: Not mechanical 'same minute' requirement.

topics.title: D Appendix: UVTA §4 and §5 Fraud/Insider Preference Causes
topics.description: The divide between all creditors and present creditors.

entries.title: §4(a)(1) actual hindrance/delay/fraud: present or future
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Transfer or obligation avoidable as to creditor whether claim arose before OR after transfer if debtor intended to hinder, delay or defraud ANY creditor.
entries.laymanExplanation: Fraudulent hiding a mansion can hurt somebody who lends later.
entries.legalExplanation: Prove actual intent from §4(b) badges, no sole test.
entries.examApplication: Use §4(b) matrix, not retroactive objective criteria alone.
entries.examTrap: Does not require insolvency as separate element.

entries.title: §4(a)(2)(i) unreasonably small assets: present or future
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Less than reasonably equivalent value, AND debtor engaged/about to engage transaction leaving remaining assets unreasonably small relative to business/transaction; both present and future may sue.
entries.laymanExplanation: Business is left unable to fund predicted expenses after undervalued transfer.
entries.legalExplanation: Capital sufficiency forward-looking; no separate actual fraud intent.
entries.examApplication: Analyze projections, capital needs and risk.
entries.examTrap: Can apply even solvent on traditional balance sheet.

entries.title: §4(a)(2)(ii) debts beyond ability to pay: present or future
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Less than reasonable value AND debtor intended, believed, or reasonably should have believed would incur debts beyond ability to pay as due.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debtor gifts property despite knowing upcoming obligations can't be met.
entries.legalExplanation: Future creditors covered even though not on scene at gift.
entries.examApplication: Track projected income/expenses and knowledge.
entries.examTrap: Requires more than hindsight bankruptcy.

entries.title: §4(b) 11 factors, nonexclusive; §4(c) burden
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Insider, retained control, concealment, suit threat, substantially all assets, abscond, removed assets, no equivalent value, insolvency, substantial debt timing, business asset-to-lienor-to-insider route; party challenging §4 bears PREPONDERANCE burden.
entries.laymanExplanation: Set of overlapping warning lights, not automatic win after X lights.
entries.legalExplanation: UVTA §4(b) 'among other factors' allows circumstances beyond enumerated eleven.
entries.examApplication: Make evidence column for each badge.
entries.examTrap: Don't say presence of one factor proves actual fraud.

entries.title: §5(a) insolvency constructive fraud: present creditors only
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Transfer/obligation to debtor's PRESENT creditor (claim already arose) if less equivalent value AND debtor insolvent at transfer or rendered insolvent.
entries.laymanExplanation: Only lenders already in line when company gave away property may use this state-law ground.
entries.legalExplanation: Different §4(a)(2) conditions available to future creditors.
entries.examApplication: For §544(b) identify actual allowable unsecured present creditor at petition.
entries.examTrap: Do not treat §5(a) as authorizing every future creditor.

entries.title: §5(b) insider preference: special PRESENT-creditor remedy
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Insider given transfer for ANTECEDENT debt, debtor insolvent, insider had reasonable cause to know insolvent, and claimant present creditor. Safe harbors §8(f), one-year §9(c).
entries.laymanExplanation: Owner gets repaid old shareholder loan while suppliers unpaid.
entries.legalExplanation: This is UVTA avoiding power separate from federal §547 and distinct from §548 insider employment category.
entries.examApplication: Identify insider status, antecedent debt, proof of awareness.
entries.examTrap: Unlike §548(a)(1)(B), doesn't require less than equivalent value.

entries.title: §5(c) claim burdens and §2(b) insolvency presumption
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Claimant must prove applicable §5(a)/(b) elements by preponderance, subject to §2(b) burden-shifting insolvency presumption.
entries.laymanExplanation: Accuser must prove case but nonpayer can face insolvency presumption.
entries.legalExplanation: Proof allocation may affect whether discovery of missing ledgers matters.
entries.examApplication: State evidentiary burden as given.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume creditors automatically win because debtor bankrupt later.

topics.title: D Appendix: UVTA §6 and §9 Transfer Timing / Extinguishment
topics.description: When transfers count as made and how long creditor may sue.

entries.title: §6(1) realty date: defeat bona fide purchaser standard
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Realty transfer made when so far perfected BFP from debtor cannot gain superior interest; sometimes recording controls.
entries.laymanExplanation: Deed signed but never recorded may not start statutory transfer clock.
entries.legalExplanation: State recording priority facts dictate whether transfer perfected under UVTA.
entries.examApplication: Use real estate purchaser priority.
entries.examTrap: Don't use simple signature date if statute postpones transfer until perfection.

entries.title: §6(1) personalty date: defeat later lien creditor standard
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Nonrealty transfer made when sufficiently perfected so ordinary creditor could not obtain superior judicial lien.
entries.laymanExplanation: Secret goods lien counts later than debtor's original security agreement.
entries.legalExplanation: Connect UCC Article9 public filing and §544(a)(1).
entries.examApplication: Timeline attachment/perfection against lien creditor.
entries.examTrap: Transfers not perfected by suit may be deemed made immediately before action §6(2).

entries.title: §6(3)–(5): no perfection, acquired rights, oral/written obligations
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: If not legally perfectible, transfer effective when between parties; no transfer before debtor owns rights in asset. Oral obligation incurred upon effective agreement; signed record when delivered to obligee.
entries.laymanExplanation: Can't transfer collateral you don't yet own for statute timing.
entries.legalExplanation: §6(2) unperfected transfer when avoidance suit filed treated immediately before action.
entries.examApplication: Track creation date, legal effectiveness and recording separately.
entries.examTrap: Do not date future-acquired collateral before debtor acquired rights.

entries.title: §9(a) actual fraud: 4 years OR 1 year discovery
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: §4(a)(1) extinguishes unless suit within four years of transfer/obligation OR, if later, within one year after actual or reasonably discoverable transfer/obligation.
entries.laymanExplanation: Hidden transfer found later may give additional one-year route for actual fraud.
entries.legalExplanation: Discovery alternative specifically actual intent claim.
entries.examApplication: For timeline use later of standard and discovery within given state model.
entries.examTrap: Not same discovery extension for every constructive fraud.

entries.title: §9(b) §4(a)(2)/§5(a): 4 years; §9(c) insider debt: 1 year
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Unreasonably small capital / inability to pay and insolvent-gift claims extinguish 4 years; insider antecedent-debt §5(b) extinguishes 1 year.
entries.laymanExplanation: Old insider repayment has much shorter special challenge window.
entries.legalExplanation: State extinguishment differs from federal action filing §546(a).
entries.examApplication: Always identify statutory subtype before counting years.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply four years to §5(b) automatically.

topics.title: D Appendix: UVTA §§7–8 Remedies and Good-Faith Defense
topics.description: Limited satisfaction, beneficiary, derivative title, special safe harbors, proof.

entries.title: §7 remedies: avoidance, attachment, injunction, receiver, execution
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Creditor may avoid to extent necessary to satisfy claim, get provisional attachment/injunction/receiver, other equitable relief, or judgment-creditor levy on asset or proceeds.
entries.laymanExplanation: Can freeze property before suspect sells it again.
entries.legalExplanation: Outside bankruptcy individual creditor recovery limited by own claim; contrast Moore v Bay whole transfer for trustee via §544(b).
entries.examApplication: Separate avoidance and later recovery.
entries.examTrap: Don't automatically give one outside creditor entire asset when smaller claim.

entries.title: §8(a) good faith + reasonably equivalent value shields ACTUAL fraud transfer
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: §4(a)(1) transfer not voidable against good-faith person who gave reasonably equivalent value to debtor or any subsequent transferee/obligee.
entries.laymanExplanation: Innocent honest collector paying full value can keep property despite seller's fraudulent intent.
entries.legalExplanation: Source Alan Drey illustrates when buyer has red flags defeating good faith.
entries.examApplication: Check consideration and red flags.
entries.examTrap: This provision is defense to §4(a)(1); other statutory protection differs.

entries.title: §8(b),(c) monetary judgment and chain of transferees
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Recovery up to LESSER transferred asset value (possibly equity-adjusted) or creditor's claim amount; defendant first transferee or benefit recipient, or immediate/mediate transferee except protected value/good-faith person and good-faith derivative successor. Value measured at transfer with equitable adjustment.
entries.laymanExplanation: If creditor owed $5k, can't get $20k cash just because property worth $20k.
entries.legalExplanation: Similar §550 but UVTA individual recovery caps claim amount.
entries.examApplication: Trace initial, intermediate, end recipient and status.
entries.examTrap: Good-faith subsequent recipient for value may shield successors in good faith.

entries.title: §8(d) innocent recipient lien/retention/offset for given value
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Good-faith transferee despite voidability entitled lien/right retain interest, enforce qualifying obligation or reduction of judgment to extent value given debtor.
entries.laymanExplanation: Someone who paid $10k in good faith may get credit for $10k even if purchase avoidable.
entries.legalExplanation: Defense protects value contributed, not necessarily full resale appraised amount.
entries.examApplication: Distinguish voidability and compensating value.
entries.examTrap: A gift recipient gave no value and receives little such protection.

entries.title: §8(e) excluded certain lease terminations and UCC collateral enforcement
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Constructive §4(a)(2)/§5 avoidance unavailable for lease termination upon contract/legal default and certain Article9 security interest enforcement except acceptance of collateral in full/partial satisfaction.
entries.laymanExplanation: Regular repossession may be insulated by special state rule.
entries.legalExplanation: Do not generalize beyond specified subsections and exceptions.
entries.examApplication: Check actual vs constructive basis.
entries.examTrap: Cannot use §8(e) to excuse deliberate secret transfer with actual intent.

entries.title: §8(f) special §5(b) insider defenses
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Insider preference excluded to extent insider supplied subsequent UNSECURED new value, transaction ordinary course, or good-faith rehabilitation securing present value and antecedent debt.
entries.laymanExplanation: Insider that supplies new money after repayment may have partial defense.
entries.legalExplanation: Compare federal §547(c)(4) new value with independent state safe harbor.
entries.examApplication: Match individual payment chronology and new value security.
entries.examTrap: A new value secured by valid lien may not count under stated exclusion.

entries.title: §8(g),(h) proof by preponderance; §10 choice of law
entries.source: Uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter9 Appendix Uniform Voidable Transactions Act (UVTA), §§1–10,12–13,15, full statutory text in user source
entries.summary: Specific parties bear proof for invoked defenses; creditor proves main cause. State governing law based on debtor's location when transfer made: individual principal residence; entity one business place or chief executive office.
entries.laymanExplanation: Need correct state's UVTA enactment, not creditor's favorite forum.
entries.legalExplanation: §12 law/equity supplements act unless displaced; §13 uniform construction; §15 name UVTA.
entries.examApplication: For conflict exam identify debtor location as of disputed transaction.
entries.examTrap: Not all defendants or businesses governed by forum-state law.
